candidates.address: Seville Place / Sherriff Street Lower, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidates.architects: John B. Keane; steeple by John Bourke
candidates.description_summary: Freestanding cruciform limestone Gothic Revival Roman Catholic church with five-bay nave, gabled transepts, chancel, four-stage tower, broach spire, pointed-arch openings, geometric tracery and stained glass.
candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH says it served the growing dockworker community and remains a local landmark/social focal point. Appraisal says begun in 1844 by John B. Keane and completed in 1858 by John Bourke; this conflicts with the survey/date-range fields and is retained as an unresolved source-internal discrepancy.

candidates.appraisal_summary: NIAH identifies the group as a local landmark with an important educational role and links it to Catholic education after Emancipation.

duplicate_screen.notes: Refreshed full-dataset scan against current main found no exact NIAH registration, normalized official title or exact address collision for the five candidates. Cross-PR review found related street/ensemble entries but no same-registration or same-property match. 50010018 is distinct from 50010033: the former is an attached 1847–48 limestone school range within the church grounds; the latter is a detached modernist school built 1936–38 on Seville Place. 50010019 and 50010018 are in the same ecclesiastical cluster as existing convent 50010020 / DUB-BLD-0194; preserve separate NIAH identities and review footprints/frontages before any import. The two Marion Terrace houses are distinct registrations and neighbouring records; PR #32 continues the terrace with Nos. 45–41. No spatial overlap is certified solely by this textual check.
